title: From balance sectors to industries
text:
1 Purpose
PEFA record energy by economic unit, classified by industry as in the national accounts (United Nations, 2019). The energy balance classifies consumption by end-use sector, that is by industrial branch, by transport mode, and for households, services and agriculture. This page links each balance flow, in the IEA template, to one or more of the 24 industries of the INS supply and use tables (SUT), or to households.
The IMF PEFA Converter (Pegoue, 2026) works at the level of ISIC sections (A, B, C, D, E, F, H, an « Other » section and households). The Tunisian industries are more detailed. Each industry therefore also carries its section, so that results can be compared with those of the tool.

import polars as pl

NOMENCLATURES = "data/nomenclatures"
SORTIE = "data/intermediaires/cles_activites.parquet"
CODES = {"code": pl.String, "activite": pl.String, "produit_cle": pl.String}

tre = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/tre.parquet")
modele = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/bilan_modele_fmi.parquet")

title: From balance sectors to industries
text:
2 Activity classification
The table data/nomenclatures/activites.csv lists the 24 SUT industries. It adds households and the four pseudo-activities of the tool. The rest of the world receives imports and exports, accumulation receives stock changes, and the environment receives natural inputs and residuals; the fourth is the statistical difference. The column section_fmi gives the matching activity code in the tool.

activites = pl.read_csv(f"{NOMENCLATURES}/activites.csv", schema_overrides=CODES)
activites.select("code", "section_fmi", "fr")

title: From balance sectors to industries
text:
3 Flow correspondence
The table data/nomenclatures/bilan_vers_activites.csv links each template flow to an activity. A row can apply to a single product, for example crude oil production or electricity losses. Rows without a product apply to all products of the flow. The column methode is direct when the flow goes entirely to one activity, and cle when it is split between several activities. The column justification explains each choice.

correspondance = pl.read_csv(f"{NOMENCLATURES}/bilan_vers_activites.csv", schema_overrides=CODES)
correspondance.filter(pl.col("methode") == "direct").select("flux_modele", "produit_modele", "activite", "justification")

Each non-zero flow of the balance must have a correspondence. Imports, exports, stock changes and the statistical difference need none, because the tool assigns them to the rest of the world and to accumulation.

PSEUDO = {"Imports", "Exports", "Stock changes", "Statistical differences"}
couverts = set(correspondance["flux_modele"])
manquants = set(modele["flux_modele"]) - couverts - PSEUDO
assert not manquants, f"Flux sans correspondance : {manquants}"
print(f"{len(set(modele['flux_modele']) - PSEUDO)} flux du bilan, tous couverts")

title: From balance sectors to industries
text:
4 Allocation keys
Two balance flows group several industries. The balance gives road transport by mode; this transport is carried out by transport firms, by all other industries and by households. The row « commerce, administration, hôtels » (trade, administration, hotels) covers about ten service industries. Their allocation follows the structure of SUT uses, in value, for a key product.

Road transport is allocated according to the uses of refined petroleum products (product 19), in the intermediate consumption of industries and in household final consumption. Refining and electricity are excluded, because their uses of product 19 are mostly transformation inputs.
Services are allocated according to the uses of electricity and gas (product 35) by the service industries.

The key of an activity is its share in the uses of the key product, among the candidate activities, for the year considered. Households take the household final consumption expenditure column.

def emplois_produit(tre: pl.DataFrame, produit: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Emplois d'un produit du TRE par branche (consommation intermédiaire) et par les ménages (MDT)."""
    emplois = tre.filter(pl.col("bloc") == "emplois", pl.col("ligne") == produit, ~pl.col("agregat"))
    return emplois.with_columns(
        activite=pl.when(pl.col("colonne") == "P3_MEN").then(pl.lit("MEN")).otherwise(pl.col("colonne"))
    ).select("annee", "activite", "valeur")


def calculer_cles(correspondance: pl.DataFrame, tre: pl.DataFrame, annees: list[int]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Facteurs de répartition par année, flux, produit et activité. Les facteurs d'un flux somment à 1."""
    directes = correspondance.filter(pl.col("methode") == "direct").join(
        pl.DataFrame({"annee": annees}, schema={"annee": pl.Int16}), how="cross"
    ).with_columns(facteur=pl.lit(1.0))
    a_repartir = correspondance.filter(pl.col("methode") == "cle")
    poids = pl.concat(
        [emplois_produit(tre, p).with_columns(produit_cle=pl.lit(p)) for p in a_repartir["produit_cle"].unique()]
    )
    reparties = (
        a_repartir.join(poids, on=["activite", "produit_cle"], how="left")
        .filter(pl.col("annee").is_in(annees))
        .with_columns(pl.col("valeur").fill_null(0))
        .with_columns(facteur=pl.col("valeur") / pl.col("valeur").sum().over("annee", "flux_modele", "produit_modele"))
    )
    colonnes = ["annee", "flux_modele", "produit_modele", "activite", "methode", "facteur"]
    return pl.concat([directes.select(colonnes), reparties.select(colonnes)]).sort(colonnes[:4])


ANNEES = sorted(modele["annee"].unique().to_list())
cles = calculer_cles(correspondance, tre, ANNEES)
sommes = cles.group_by("annee", "flux_modele", "produit_modele").agg(pl.col("facteur").sum())
assert (sommes["facteur"] - 1).abs().max() < 1e-9, "Les facteurs d'un flux doivent sommer à 1"

The following table gives the road transport keys, in percent, for a few years.

(
    cles.filter(pl.col("flux_modele") == "Road", pl.col("annee").is_in([2015, 2019, 2022]))
    .with_columns((pl.col("facteur") * 100).round(1))
    .pivot("annee", index="activite", values="facteur")
    .join(activites.select(pl.col("code").alias("activite"), "fr"), on="activite")
    .sort("2022", descending=True)
)







NoteOpen question



The road transport key rests on the value of petroleum products bought by each industry and by households. It mixes fuel with other uses (liquefied petroleum gas for cooking, fuel oil for heat). A survey of fuel use by vehicle type and user, if one exists at INS or ANME, would give a more accurate allocation.


The services keys follow.

(
    cles.filter(pl.col("flux_modele") == "Commercial and public services", pl.col("annee").is_in([2015, 2019, 2022]))
    .with_columns((pl.col("facteur") * 100).round(1))
    .pivot("annee", index="activite", values="facteur")
    .join(activites.select(pl.col("code").alias("activite"), "fr"), on="activite")
    .sort("2022", descending=True)
)

5 Saving

cles.write_parquet(SORTIE, compression="zstd")
print(f"{SORTIE} : {cles.height} lignes, années {ANNEES[0]} à {ANNEES[-1]}")

title: Extracting the supply and use tables
text:
1 Purpose
The National Institute of Statistics (INS) provided the supply and use tables (SUT) from 2015 to 2023, at current prices, in million dinars (million TND). There is one sheet per year. The SUT give the energy and emissions accounts their list of 24 industries. The uses of products 06, 19 and 35 provide keys to allocate energy between industries. Output and value added by industry feed the intensity indicators. This page brings the nine sheets together in data/intermediaires/tre.parquet.
The functions are in the script scripts/extraire_tre.py1, which this page imports and runs.

import sys

import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import extraire_tre as et

et.feuilles()

title: Extracting the supply and use tables
text:
2 Structure of a sheet
Each sheet places three blocks side by side on the same product rows.

The supply table: output, imports, taxes and subsidies on products, margins, CIF/FOB adjustment, total supply.
The intermediate consumption matrix: one column per industry, with the industry code as header. Industry codes are the same as product codes.
Final uses: final consumption of households and general government, gross fixed capital formation, changes in inventories, exports.

Below the matrix, five rows give the production accounts of the industries: output, value added, compensation of employees, net taxes on production, gross operating surplus.
The sheets for 2015 to 2018 and those for 2019 to 2023 do not have the same columns. The latter have one more label column and a column « Somme des Emplois » (total uses). The script therefore finds each column by the text of its header, never by its position. The table data/nomenclatures/tre_colonnes.csv links each header to a System of National Accounts code and flags the subtotal columns. An unknown header stops the reading.

pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/tre_colonnes.csv").select("libelle_source", "code", "bloc", "agregat")

Products and industries are described in data/nomenclatures/tre_produits.csv. Rows CR2 and CR3 are adjustment rows, for the territorial adjustment and the CIF/FOB adjustment.

pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/tre_produits.csv", schema_overrides={"code": pl.String}).select("code", "fr", "en")

title: Extracting the supply and use tables
text:
3 Long format
The long table has one row per year, block, row and column. The column ligne holds the product code, or the aggregate code for the value added rows. The column colonne holds the industry code for the intermediate consumption matrix and the value added rows, and the transaction code for the other columns. The column agregat flags the published subtotals, which serve for checks and must not be added to the details.

tre = et.extraire()
tre.filter(pl.col("annee") == 2022, pl.col("ligne") == "35", ~pl.col("agregat")).sort("valeur", descending=True).head(8)

title: Extracting the supply and use tables
text:
4 Checks
Supply and use balance. For each product and each year, the published total supply must equal the sum of detailed supply and the sum of detailed uses.

equilibre = et.ecarts_equilibre(tre)
resume = equilibre.group_by("annee").agg(
    pl.col("ecart_ressources").abs().max().round(3),
    pl.col("ecart_emplois").abs().max().round(3),
).sort("annee")
assert resume["ecart_ressources"].max() < 1 and resume["ecart_emplois"].max() < 1, "TRE déséquilibré"
resume

Production accounts. For each industry, output must equal intermediate consumption plus value added.

production = et.ecarts_production(tre)
assert production["ecart"].abs().max() < 1, "Compte de production déséquilibré"
production.group_by("annee").agg(pl.col("ecart").abs().max().round(3).alias("ecart_max_mdt")).sort("annee")

The differences are below one million dinars and come from the rounding of the values.

title: Extracting the supply and use tables
text:
5 Saving

et.SORTIE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
tre.write_parquet(et.SORTIE, compression="zstd")
print(f"{et.SORTIE} : {tre.height} lignes, {tre['annee'].n_unique()} années")

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
1 Purpose
The National Observatory of Energy and Mines (ONEM) publishes one energy balance per year, in thousand tonnes of oil equivalent (ktoe). The eight workbooks from 2015 to 2022 follow the same logic, but their layout changes from one year to the next. This page brings them together in a single long table, with a stable code for each flow and each product. This table, data/intermediaires/bilans_energetiques.parquet, is the starting point of the physical energy flow accounts (PEFA).
The functions are in the script scripts/extraire_bilans.py1, which this page imports and runs step by step. The same script can be run on its own with uv run python scripts/extraire_bilans.py.

import sys

import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import extraire_bilans as eb

fichiers = eb.fichiers_bilans()
{annee: chemin.name for annee, chemin in fichiers.items()}

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
2 Reading a balance
Each workbook has a single sheet. Product names take up two header rows, starting at the row whose first cell begins with « en 1000 tep ». The function lire_bilan joins these two rows into one label, reads the flows from « Production primaire » (primary production) onwards and puts the table in long format. Empty cells are zeros and are dropped. One 2015 cell contains « 0 * », with a footnote mark; the asterisk is removed.
Some flow labels repeat. « Raffineries » (refineries) appears in both the transformation inputs and the transformation outputs, and « Chimie » (chemicals) appears in both non-energy consumption and industry. The column bloc keeps the last block title found above each row, which removes the ambiguity.

exemple = eb.lire_bilan(fichiers[2022], 2022)
exemple.filter(pl.col("flux_source") == "Raffineries", pl.col("produit_source") == "Pétrole brut")

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
3 Layout drift between years
The workbooks do not all have the same columns or rows. The following table counts the distinct labels of each year.

lus = pl.concat([eb.lire_bilan(chemin, annee) for annee, chemin in fichiers.items()])
lus.group_by("annee").agg(
    pl.col("produit_source").n_unique().alias("colonnes de produits"),
    pl.col("flux_source").n_unique().alias("libellés de flux"),
).sort("annee")

The main differences are listed below.

In 2015, the natural gas liquids column is called « GPL primaire » (primary LPG), and the « Gaz de raffinage » (refinery gas) column does not exist.
In 2016, a « géothermie » (geothermal) column is added to the renewable energies. It is the extra column of that year.
In several years, the headers for wind and hydro energy are shifted across the two rows. Reading gives « Energie éolienne hydraulique » for wind and « Energie » for hydro; the primary production values confirm this reading.
In 2015, industry has three rows, « Sidérurgie » (iron and steel), « Métaux non ferreux » (non-ferrous metals) and « Fabrications métalliques » (metal products). The following years have a single row « Fabrications métalliques y compris sidérurgie » (metal products including iron and steel). The row « Fabrications mécaniques et électriques » (mechanical and electrical products) has values only from 2019.
Several labels change spelling (« Soutess internationales », « Consommation intérieur brute », « Agriculture » and later « Agriculture et pêche »).

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
4 Assigning codes
Labels do not serve as identifiers. Two lookup tables, edited by hand, link each original label to a code.

data/nomenclatures/bilan_flux_sources.csv links a pair (block, label) to a flow code.
data/nomenclatures/bilan_produits_sources.csv links a product label to a product code.

The codes are described in data/nomenclatures/bilan_flux.csv and data/nomenclatures/bilan_produits.csv, with their labels in French, English and Arabic, their parent aggregate and, for flows, the sign of their contribution to that aggregate. The column a_verifier flags the translations to be reviewed by the Tunisian counterparts.

pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/bilan_flux.csv").select("code", "parent", "signe", "fr", "en")


pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/bilan_produits.csv").select("code", "parent", "fr", "en")

The function coder joins the two tables and stops if a label has no code. A new balance whose layout changes again therefore raises an explicit error, instead of a silent shift.
In 2015, « Sidérurgie », « Métaux non ferreux » and « Fabrications métalliques » all receive the code IND_MET. The function agreger adds up the rows that share a code and keeps the original labels. The 2015 sum is of the same order as the single row of the following years, which supports this choice.

bilans = eb.extraire()
(
    bilans.filter(pl.col("code_flux").is_in(["IND_MET", "IND_MEC"]), pl.col("code_produit") == "TOTAL")
    .pivot("code_flux", index="annee", values="ktep")
    .sort("annee")
)







NoteOpen question



The 2015 row « Fabrications métalliques » could correspond to mechanical and electrical products, as its position in the table suggests. It is classified here with iron and steel, because mechanical and electrical products have no value before 2019. To be confirmed with ONEM.

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
5 Conversion to terajoules
PEFA are expressed in terajoules (TJ). One tonne of oil equivalent equals 41.868 GJ, so one ktoe equals 41.868 TJ (United Nations, 2019).

bilans.head(6)

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
6 Checks
The balance publishes values rounded to the ktoe, sometimes to one decimal. The checks therefore allow a difference of 2 ktoe.
Flow aggregates. Each aggregate (industry, transport, transformation inputs, gross inland consumption, etc.) must equal the signed sum of its components, for each product and each year. For example, gross inland consumption equals primary production, plus imports and stock changes, minus exports and international bunkers.
Product aggregates. The column « Total tous produits » (total, all products) must equal the sum of the first-level products, and the columns for petroleum products and renewable energies must equal the sum of their products.
Available for final consumption. For each product, it must equal gross inland consumption, minus transformation inputs, plus transformation outputs and exchanges, minus energy sector own use and losses.

TOLERANCE = 2.0
controles = {
    "Agrégats de flux": eb.ecarts_hierarchie(bilans, "flux"),
    "Agrégats de produits": eb.ecarts_hierarchie(bilans, "produit"),
    "Disponible pour la consommation finale": eb.ecarts_identites(bilans),
}
resume = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "controle": list(controles),
        "cellules": [t.height for t in controles.values()],
        "ecart_max_ktep": [t["ecart"].abs().max() for t in controles.values()],
        "ecarts_sup_1_ktep": [t.filter(pl.col("ecart").abs() > 1).height for t in controles.values()],
    }
)
assert (resume["ecart_max_ktep"] <= TOLERANCE).all(), "Écart supérieur à la tolérance : vérifier la lecture"
resume

The few differences above one ktoe are listed below. They come from the rounding of the published values.

pl.concat(
    [t.rename({c: "element" for c in t.columns if c.startswith("code_")}).select(
        pl.lit(nom).alias("controle"), "annee", pl.col("element"), pl.col("ecart").round(2)
    ) for nom, t in controles.items()]
).filter(pl.col("ecart").abs() > 1).sort("annee")

title: Extracting the energy balances
text:
7 Saving
The table is saved in Parquet, compressed with zstd. It keeps the original labels next to the codes, for traceability.

eb.SORTIE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
bilans.write_parquet(eb.SORTIE, compression="zstd")
print(f"{eb.SORTIE} : {bilans.height} lignes, {bilans['annee'].n_unique()} années")

title: Energy and air emissions accounts for Tunisia
text:
This site gathers the materials that support the compilation of physical energy flow accounts (PEFA) and air emissions accounts (AEA) for Tunisia. The work is carried out by the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and partner institutions, with technical assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Materials are published as the mission progresses.
The site is available in French, English and Arabic. The French version is the reference version. The “Language” menu opens the same page in another language.

Contents
Materials. The documents and presentations cover the mission context, the SEEA framework and the compilation methods.
Processing. The processing pages describe step by step, with Python code, how the source data become accounts. Each page ends with the export of its tables.
Downloads. The downloads page collects the final tables in Excel format, in French, English and Arabic.


Objectives

Move from the national energy balance to physical energy supply and use tables.
Move from the national greenhouse gas inventory to air emissions accounts by economic activity.
Keep a complete and reproducible record of data, methods and code.
Prepare a workplan for the dissemination of the accounts.

title: About
text:
This site
This site is part of the technical assistance that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) provides to national statistical offices on the compilation of environmental and economic statistics. In Tunisia, the work with the National Institute of Statistics (INS) covers the energy and air emissions accounts of the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA).
The materials document the process and leave resources that institutions can consult and adapt to their own context. They are updated as the work progresses, so their content may change.


Reproducibility
All processing is written in Python in Quarto documents that interleave text and code. The environment is described in pyproject.toml and locked by uv.lock, so anyone can reproduce the results with uv sync. The source code is available in the GitHub repository.
The French processing pages run the code. The English and Arabic versions show the same code without running it, so that calculations are not repeated.


Author
The content was prepared by Renato Vargas, economist and IMF consultant.

title: Introduction to energy and air emissions accounts
text:
The SEEA Central Framework
The System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) records flows between the environment and the economy in supply and use tables consistent with the System of National Accounts (United Nations et al., 2014).

PEFA describe energy flows in terajoules (United Nations, 2019).
AEA attribute emissions to resident industries and households (Eurostat, 2015).

title: Mission context
text:
The technical assistance responds to a request from the Tunisian authorities for support on the compilation of air emissions accounts. It is part of the climate statistics programme of the IMF Statistics Department and involves the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and the relevant ministries.
In June 2026, Tunisian representatives took part in a three-day virtual workshop on energy and air emissions accounts. The workshop covered the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) framework, energy balances and energy accounts, air emissions inventories and accounts, data requirements and compilation issues (Eurostat, 2015; United Nations et al., 2014; United Nations, 2019). The Tunisian participants presented their work and data (Besbes, 2026; Bouazizi, 2026).

The technical assistance responds to a request from the Tunisian authorities for support on the compilation of air emissions accounts. It is part of the climate statistics programme of the IMF Statistics Department and involves the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and the relevant ministries.

The workshop covered the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) framework, energy balances and energy accounts, air emissions inventories and accounts, data requirements and compilation issues (Eurostat, 2015; United Nations et al., 2014; United Nations, 2019). The Tunisian participants presented their work and data (Besbes, 2026; Bouazizi, 2026).

title: Mission context
section: 2 The energy and emissions statistical system
text:
2 The energy and emissions statistical system
The National Observatory of Energy and Mines (ONEM), under the ministry in charge of energy, produces the national energy balance. Tunisia has compiled a balance since the 1980s and has published it every year in the Eurostat and International Energy Agency format since 2010 (Bouazizi, 2026). The INS compiles and disseminates official statistics, including energy indicators and the national accounts.
The National Agency for Energy Conservation (ANME) coordinates the national greenhouse gas inventory for the energy and industrial processes sectors. The Ministry of Agriculture coordinates agriculture and land use, and the National Sanitation Office (ONAS) coordinates waste. The inventory covers 1990 to 2022, with an estimate for 2023, follows the 2006 IPCC Guidelines and uses the global warming potentials of the Fifth Assessment Report (Besbes, 2026; Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, 2006).
The INS reported three difficulties at the workshop (Bouazizi, 2026). The classifications of the energy balance and of economic activities are not always harmonised. Energy consumption by product and by sector has gaps and relies on estimates. The national accounts cover the informal sector, while the balance does not.

title: Mission context
text:
4 IMF tools
The IMF has developed two tools for these accounts. The PEFA Converter transforms an energy balance into physical energy supply and use tables using a concordance matrix between balance flows and industries (International Monetary Fund, 2024). The I2A converter transforms an emissions inventory into air emissions accounts by economic activity, with a residence adjustment for air and water transport. Both tools combine an Excel workbook with Python functions.
The processing pages of this site follow the same steps in documents that describe each operation and its code.

The mission takes place in Tunis from 7 to 11 December 2026. Table 2 lists the topics planned for each day.

Energy accounts framework: activity and product classifications, allocation matrix, residence and territory adjustment, consistency checks. Compilation and dissemination of energy accounts.

Institutional arrangements and data sources for air emissions accounts. Air emissions accounts framework: activity and source classifications, allocation matrix, residence and territory adjustment, consistency checks. Compilation and dissemination.

Note



This page shows the code of the French reference page without running it. Results and outputs are in the French page. Code comments stay in French.

title: Reading the energy balance
text:
1 Purpose
This page is the template for the processing pages. It reads the 2022 energy balance, converts it to long format, converts thousand tonnes of oil equivalent (ktoe) to terajoules (TJ) and exports the result. The Parquet table feeds the following pages, and the Excel workbooks in three languages are published on the downloads page.
Paths are relative to the project root, because _quarto.yml sets execute-dir: project.

title: Reading the energy balance
text:
2 Libraries and parameters

from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import xlsxwriter

ANNEE = 2022
SOURCE = Path("data/sources/bilan-energetique/balance2022.xlsx")
INTERMEDIAIRES = Path("data/intermediaires")
PRODUITS = Path("data/produits")

# Facteur de conversion : 1 tep = 41,868 GJ, donc 1 ktep = 41,868 TJ
KTEP_EN_TJ = 41.868

title: Reading the energy balance
text:
3 Reading the workbook
The ONEM workbook places product names on two header rows and flows in the first column. The polars library reads the sheet without a header; empty rows at the top of the sheet are skipped on reading.

brut = pl.read_excel(SOURCE, has_header=False, engine="calamine", infer_schema_length=0)

# Les deux lignes d'en-tête des produits commencent par « en 1000 tep »
ligne_entete = brut.with_row_index().filter(
    pl.col("column_0").str.starts_with("en 1000 tep")
)["index"][0]


def nom_produit(haut: str | None, bas: str | None) -> str:
    """Réunit les deux lignes d'en-tête d'un produit en un seul libellé."""
    morceaux = [m.strip() for m in (haut, bas) if m is not None and m.strip()]
    return " ".join(" ".join(morceaux).split())


produits = [
    nom_produit(brut[ligne_entete, j], brut[ligne_entete + 1, j])
    for j in range(1, brut.width)
]
produits[:6]

Flows start at the “Production primaire” row. Some labels repeat: “Raffineries” appears in both transformation inputs and transformation outputs. The section column keeps the title of the block each row belongs to, and the ordre column keeps its position in the balance.

SECTIONS = {
    "Entrées en transformation",
    "Sortie de transformation",
    "Echanges, transfer, restitutions",
    "Consommation finale non énergétique",
    "Consommation finale énergétique",
    "Industrie",
    "Transport",
    "Foyers domestiques, commerce, adm, etc.",
}

debut = brut.with_row_index().filter(pl.col("column_0") == "Production primaire")["index"][0]
corps = brut[debut:].rename(
    {f"column_{j}": produits[j - 1] for j in range(1, brut.width)} | {"column_0": "flux"}
)


def attribuer_sections(flux: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Associe chaque ligne au dernier titre de bloc rencontré au-dessus d'elle."""
    courante, resultat = "Approvisionnement", []
    for libelle in flux:
        if libelle in SECTIONS:
            courante = libelle
        resultat.append(courante)
    return resultat


corps = corps.with_columns(
    pl.Series("section", attribuer_sections(corps["flux"].to_list())),
    pl.Series("ordre", range(1, corps.height + 1)),
)
corps.select("ordre", "section", "flux").head(12)

title: Reading the energy balance
text:
4 Long format and conversion
The long format has one row per flow and product. Empty cells in the balance are zeros and are dropped.

bilan = (
    corps.unpivot(index=["ordre", "section", "flux"], variable_name="produit", value_name="ktep")
    .with_columns(pl.col("ktep").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False))
    .filter(pl.col("ktep").is_not_null() & (pl.col("ktep") != 0))
    .with_columns(
        pl.lit(ANNEE).alias("annee"),
        (pl.col("ktep") * KTEP_EN_TJ).alias("tj"),
    )
    .select("annee", "ordre", "section", "flux", "produit", "ktep", "tj")
)
bilan.head(8)

title: Reading the energy balance
text:
5 Check
Primary production in the “Total tous produits” column must equal the sum of the product columns, excluding subtotal columns. This check confirms that reading did not shift any column. The tolerance is one ktoe, because the balance publishes rounded values.

production = bilan.filter(pl.col("flux") == "Production primaire")
total = production.filter(pl.col("produit") == "Total tous produits")["ktep"][0]
somme = production.filter(~pl.col("produit").str.starts_with("Total"))["ktep"].sum()
assert abs(total - somme) < 1, f"Écart de {total - somme:.1f} ktep : vérifier les colonnes"
print(f"Production primaire : total {total:,.0f} ktep, somme des produits {somme:,.1f} ktep")
print(f"Soit {total * KTEP_EN_TJ:,.0f} TJ")

title: Reading the energy balance
text:
6 Export
The intermediate table is saved as Parquet with zstd compression. The Excel workbooks contain the same table with headers translated from data/nomenclatures/libelles.csv. The Arabic sheet runs right to left. Flow and product labels stay in French on this example page; their translation belongs to the classifications still to be built.

INTERMEDIAIRES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
bilan.write_parquet(INTERMEDIAIRES / f"bilan_energetique_{ANNEE}.parquet", compression="zstd")

libelles = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/libelles.csv")


def exporter_excel(tableau: pl.DataFrame, langue: str, nom: str) -> Path:
    """Écrit un classeur Excel avec les en-têtes dans la langue demandée."""
    traduction = dict(zip(libelles["cle"], libelles[langue]))
    dossier = PRODUITS / langue
    dossier.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    chemin = dossier / f"{nom}.xlsx"
    feuille = f"{traduction['feuille_bilan']} {ANNEE}"
    with xlsxwriter.Workbook(chemin) as classeur:
        tableau.rename({c: traduction.get(c, c) for c in tableau.columns}).write_excel(
            workbook=classeur, worksheet=feuille, autofit=True, float_precision=1
        )
        if langue == "ar":
            classeur.get_worksheet_by_name(feuille).right_to_left()
    return chemin


for langue in ["fr", "en", "ar"]:
    print(exporter_excel(bilan, langue, f"bilan_energetique_{ANNEE}"))

The following buttons download the workbooks.
English Français العربية

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory
text:
Note



This page shows the code of the French reference page without running it. Results and outputs are in the French page. Code comments stay in French.

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory
text:
1 Purpose
Tunisia reports its greenhouse gas inventory to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in the Common Reporting Tables (CRT). There is one workbook per year, from 2015 to 2022. The Data sheet of each workbook already holds all values in long format, with one row per CRT category, parameter, type, fuel and gas. This page stacks the eight sheets into data/intermediaires/crt.parquet, which will feed the air emissions accounts (AEA).
The functions are in the script scripts/extraire_crt.py1, which this page imports and runs.

import sys

import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import extraire_crt as ec

{annee: chemin.name for annee, chemin in ec.fichiers_crt().items()}

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory
text:
2 Structure of the Data sheet
The sheet has eight columns. They are renamed in French. The column valeur is read as text and then converted to a number.

pl.DataFrame({"colonne CRT": list(ec.COLONNES), "nom retenu": list(ec.COLONNES.values())})

The parameter distinguishes three kinds of rows. The activity rows give activity data, for example fuel consumption in TJ. The emission rows give emissions, in kilotonnes (kt) of each gas. The information rows give emission factors and other context data.

crt, doublons = ec.extraire()
crt.filter(pl.col("annee") == 2022).group_by("parametre", "unite").len().sort("len", descending=True).head(8)

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory
text:
3 Duplicate rows
Each Data sheet contains rows that are exactly identical and repeated. They are removed, because a sum would count them twice. The following table gives the number of rows removed per year.

pl.DataFrame({"annee": list(doublons), "lignes_retirees": list(doublons.values())})

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory
text:
4 Check against the Summary2 table
The Summary2 sheet of each workbook gives emissions by category and gas, in kt of CO2 equivalent. The check sums the Data emissions of each category, gas by gas, and converts them to CO2 equivalent with the 100-year global warming potentials of the IPCC Fifth Assessment Report, which the Tunisian inventory uses (CH4: 28, N2O: 265). Memo items (category 1.D, international bunkers) are excluded from the energy totals, as in Summary2.

comparaisons = pl.concat([ec.comparer_summary2(crt, a).with_columns(annee=pl.lit(a)) for a in sorted(doublons)])
resume = comparaisons.group_by("annee").agg(
    pl.len().alias("cellules"),
    pl.col("ecart").abs().max().round(4).alias("ecart_max"),
    (pl.col("ecart").abs() > 0.01).sum().alias("ecarts_sup_0_01"),
).sort("annee")
assert resume["ecart_max"].max() < 1, "Écart important avec Summary2 : vérifier la lecture"
resume

The Data values reproduce Summary2 for all categories from 2015 to 2018. From 2019, a single difference appears, in the N2O emissions of category 1.B.2 (fugitive emissions from oil and natural gas), and it carries over to its aggregates.

comparaisons.filter(pl.col("ecart").abs() > 0.01).select("annee", "crt", "gaz", pl.col("ecart").round(3))


crt.filter(
    pl.col("crt") == "1.B.2.b.ii", pl.col("gaz") == "N2O", pl.col("parametre") == "emission", pl.col("valeur") != 0
).select("annee", "crt", "combustible", "valeur")







NoteOpen question



The N2O emissions of category 1.B.2.b.ii appear in the Data sheet from 2019 but are not counted in Summary2. The difference is less than one kilotonne of CO2 equivalent. To be clarified with the inventory team (ANME).

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory
text:
5 Saving

ec.SORTIE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
crt.write_parquet(ec.SORTIE, compression="zstd")
print(f"{ec.SORTIE} : {crt.height} lignes, {crt['annee'].n_unique()} années")

title: Extracting the greenhouse gas inventory

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template
text:
1 Purpose
The IMF PEFA Converter (International Monetary Fund, 2024; Pegoue, 2026) reads an energy balance laid out like those of the International Energy Agency (IEA), with 95 flows in a fixed order, 63 products, values in terajoules (TJ) and IEA signs. This page transfers the ONEM balances from 2015 to 2022 into that template. The result, data/intermediaires/bilan_modele_fmi.parquet, feeds both calculations of the PEFA, the call to the IMF tool and its explicit re-implementation in polars.

import sys

import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import outils_fmi as of

NOMENCLATURES = "data/nomenclatures"
SORTIE = "data/intermediaires/bilan_modele_fmi.parquet"

bilans = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/bilans_energetiques.parquet")

The module scripts/outils_fmi.py1 reads the lists of flows and products from the Energy_Balance_Template sheet of the tool workbook.

FLUX_MODELE = of.lignes_flux_modele()
PRODUITS_MODELE = [p for p in of.produits_modele() if p != "Total"]
print(f"{len(FLUX_MODELE)} flux et {len(PRODUITS_MODELE)} produits dans le modèle")
FLUX_MODELE[:12]

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template
text:
2 Sign conventions
The ONEM balance publishes all flows as positive values and combines them by addition or subtraction. The IEA template carries the sign in the value. Exports, international bunkers, transformation inputs, energy sector own use and losses are negative there. Stock changes keep the ONEM sign, because both balances add them to supply.
The statistical difference changes sign. In the ONEM balance, the amount available for final consumption equals final consumption plus the statistical difference. In the IEA template, the statistical difference is added to supply to equal final consumption. The IEA difference is therefore the opposite of the ONEM one.

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template
text:
3 Correspondences
Each elementary flow of the balance receives a template flow and a sign, in the columns flux_modele and signe_modele of data/nomenclatures/bilan_flux.csv. Each elementary product receives a template product in the column produit_modele of data/nomenclatures/bilan_produits.csv. The balance aggregates (gross inland consumption, total petroleum products, etc.) have no correspondence, because the template recomputes them.

flux = pl.read_csv(f"{NOMENCLATURES}/bilan_flux.csv")
flux.filter(pl.col("flux_modele").is_not_null()).select("code", "fr", "flux_modele", "signe_modele")


produits = pl.read_csv(f"{NOMENCLATURES}/bilan_produits.csv")
produits.filter(pl.col("produit_modele").is_not_null()).select("code", "fr", "produit_modele")

Some cells of the balance need special treatment. They are listed, with their justification, in data/nomenclatures/bilan_vers_modele_exceptions.csv. An exception replaces the default flow, product or sign for a specific (flow, product) pair.

exceptions = pl.read_csv(f"{NOMENCLATURES}/bilan_vers_modele_exceptions.csv")
exceptions

Two points need explaining. The ONEM balance records electricity generation from wind, solar and hydro as an exchange between products, in which the primary production of each source moves to electricity. The IEA template treats these sources as inputs to power plants, and the electricity generated as an output. The exceptions therefore move these exchanges to the power plant row. The ONEM balance also places charcoal production in the biomass column; its output becomes the template product « Charcoal ».






NoteOpen question



Energy sector own use is not broken down by industry in the balance. Natural gas, gas oil and natural gas liquids are assigned to oil and gas extraction, fuel oil and refinery gas to the refinery, and electricity to power plants. This allocation is to be confirmed with ONEM.

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template
text:
4 Transfer
The following function applies the default correspondences, then the exceptions, and changes the signs. The TJ values come from the extraction of the balances. Aggregate cells are left aside. The conservation check, further below, verifies that no elementary cell is lost.

def transposer(bilans: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Transpose le bilan long de l'ONEM dans les flux et produits du modèle de l'AIE (TJ, signes de l'AIE)."""
    defaut = (
        bilans.join(
            flux.select(pl.col("code").alias("code_flux"), "flux_modele", "signe_modele"), on="code_flux"
        )
        .join(produits.select(pl.col("code").alias("code_produit"), "produit_modele"), on="code_produit")
        # Seules les cellules élémentaires (flux et produit non agrégés) sont transposées.
        .filter(pl.col("flux_modele").is_not_null() & pl.col("produit_modele").is_not_null())
    )

    regles = exceptions.select(
        "code_flux", "code_produit",
        pl.col("flux_modele").alias("flux_exc"),
        pl.col("produit_modele").alias("produit_exc"),
        pl.col("signe_modele").cast(pl.Int8).alias("signe_exc"),
    )
    return (
        defaut.join(regles, on=["code_flux", "code_produit"], how="left")
        .with_columns(
            flux_modele=pl.coalesce("flux_exc", "flux_modele"),
            produit_modele=pl.coalesce("produit_exc", "produit_modele"),
            signe_modele=pl.coalesce("signe_exc", "signe_modele"),
        )
        .with_columns(tj=pl.col("tj") * pl.col("signe_modele"))
        .select("annee", "code_flux", "code_produit", "flux_modele", "produit_modele", "tj")
    )


modele = transposer(bilans)
inconnus = set(modele["flux_modele"]) - set(FLUX_MODELE) | set(modele["produit_modele"]) - set(PRODUITS_MODELE)
assert not inconnus, f"Libellés absents du modèle : {inconnus}"
modele.filter(pl.col("annee") == 2022, pl.col("code_produit") == "GN").head(8)

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template
text:
5 Checks
Conservation. Each elementary cell of the balance is found in the template, apart from the unit conversion. The sum of absolute values is therefore the same before and after the transfer.

KTEP_EN_TJ = 41.868
elementaires = bilans.filter(
    pl.col("code_flux").is_in(flux.filter(pl.col("flux_modele").is_not_null())["code"].implode()),
    pl.col("code_produit").is_in(produits.filter(pl.col("produit_modele").is_not_null())["code"].implode()),
)
avant = elementaires.group_by("annee").agg((pl.col("ktep").abs().sum() * KTEP_EN_TJ).alias("avant_tj"))
apres = modele.group_by("annee").agg(pl.col("tj").abs().sum().alias("apres_tj"))
conservation = avant.join(apres, on="annee").with_columns(ecart=pl.col("avant_tj") - pl.col("apres_tj")).sort("annee")
assert conservation["ecart"].abs().max() < 1e-6
conservation

IEA identity. For each ONEM product, supply, transfers, the statistical difference, transformation, energy sector own use and losses, with their signs, must add up to final consumption. The check is done by ONEM product, because biomass feeds two template products (wood and charcoal). The check adds up about forty cells rounded to the ktoe, rather than published aggregates as in the extraction. The tolerance is therefore 3 ktoe, about 126 TJ. It is reached only for natural gas in 2017 and 2018.

CONSOMMATION_FINALE = flux.filter(
    pl.col("code").str.starts_with("IND_") | pl.col("code").str.starts_with("TRA_")
    | pl.col("code").str.starts_with("AUT_") | pl.col("code").str.starts_with("CFNE_")
)["code"].to_list()
identite = (
    modele.with_columns(finale=pl.col("code_flux").is_in(CONSOMMATION_FINALE))
    .group_by("annee", "code_produit")
    .agg(
        pl.col("tj").filter(~pl.col("finale")).sum().alias("ressources_nettes"),
        pl.col("tj").filter(pl.col("finale")).sum().alias("consommation_finale"),
    )
    .with_columns(ecart_tj=pl.col("ressources_nettes") - pl.col("consommation_finale"))
)
assert identite["ecart_tj"].abs().max() < 3 * KTEP_EN_TJ + 1e-6, "Identité de l'AIE non vérifiée"
identite.group_by("annee").agg(pl.col("ecart_tj").abs().max().round(1).alias("ecart_max_tj")).sort("annee")

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template
text:
6 The 2022 balance in the template
The following table shows the 2022 balance in the template, in thousand TJ (PJ), for the products present. The aggregate rows of the template are left empty, because the tool does not use them.

apercu = (
    modele.filter(pl.col("annee") == 2022)
    .group_by("flux_modele", "produit_modele")
    .agg((pl.col("tj").sum() / 1000).round(1).alias("pj"))
    .pivot("produit_modele", index="flux_modele", values="pj")
)
ordre = {f: i for i, f in enumerate(FLUX_MODELE)}
apercu.sort(pl.col("flux_modele").replace_strict(ordre, return_dtype=pl.Int32))

title: The ONEM balance in the PEFA Converter template

7 Saving
The long table keeps the ONEM codes next to the template labels. Several ONEM cells can end up in the same template cell (for example the three exchange rows), and the function outils_fmi.bilan_vers_plage adds them up when it builds the tool range.

modele.write_parquet(SORTIE, compression="zstd")
print(f"{SORTIE} : {modele.height} lignes")

title: Concordance matrix and bridging items
text:
1 Purpose
The concordance matrix of the PEFA Converter (International Monetary Fund, 2024; Pegoue, 2026) states, for each flow and product of the balance, to which PEFA product, activity and quadrant (supply or use) the energy is assigned, and in what proportion. The matrix supplied with the tool assigns each flow to an ISIC section. This page builds a Tunisian matrix by SUT industry, from the default matrix and the correspondences of the previous page, and documents each difference. It also deals with the bridging items between the balance and the accounts, namely international bunkers and residence adjustments.

import sys

import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import outils_fmi as of

CODES = {"code": pl.String, "activite": pl.String, "produit_cle": pl.String}
SORTIE = "data/intermediaires/concordance_tunisie.parquet"

activites = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/activites.csv", schema_overrides=CODES)
correspondance = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/bilan_vers_activites.csv", schema_overrides=CODES)
cles = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/cles_activites.parquet")
modele = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/bilan_modele_fmi.parquet")

title: Concordance matrix and bridging items
text:
2 The default matrix
The module scripts/outils_fmi.py1 reads the named range Concordance_Matrix of the tool workbook, as Excel passes it to the function EB2PEFA. The matrix has one row per flow, product and target activity. The tool itself rescales the allocation factors to a sum of 1 per flow, product, target product and quadrant.

plages = of.plages_classeur()
COLONNES_CM = plages["CM"][0]


def matrice_en_polars(plage: list[list]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Convertit la plage Concordance_Matrix en tableau polars ; les facteurs non numériques valent 0, comme dans l'outil."""
    tableau = pl.DataFrame(plage[1:], schema=[str(c) for c in plage[0]], orient="row", infer_schema_length=None)
    return tableau.with_columns(pl.col("Allocation Factor").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False).fill_null(0))


defaut = matrice_en_polars(plages["CM"])
print(f"{defaut.height} lignes, colonnes : {', '.join(defaut.columns)}")
defaut.filter(pl.col("EB_Flow") == "Road", pl.col("EB_Product") == "Motor gasoline excl. biofuels")

title: Concordance matrix and bridging items
text:
3 The Tunisian matrix
The Tunisian matrix keeps all columns of the default matrix and changes only the target activity and the factor. For each flow covered by data/nomenclatures/bilan_vers_activites.csv, the default rows are replaced by one row per Tunisian activity, with the key of the year as factor. A product-specific correspondence (for example crude oil losses) takes precedence over the general correspondence of the flow. Flows absent from the Tunisian balance and the pseudo-activities of the tool (rest of the world, accumulation) keep the default matrix.
The road transport and services keys change every year. There is therefore one matrix per year.

def matrice_tunisienne(defaut: pl.DataFrame, cles_annee: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Remplace l'activité et le facteur des flux couverts par les clés tunisiennes d'une année."""
    flux_couverts = cles_annee["flux_modele"].unique()
    specifiques = cles_annee.filter(pl.col("produit_modele").is_not_null())
    generales = cles_annee.filter(pl.col("produit_modele").is_null()).drop("produit_modele")

    a_remplacer = defaut.filter(pl.col("EB_Flow").is_in(flux_couverts.implode()))
    # Une ligne par flux, produit et quadrant suffit comme gabarit : les autres colonnes sont identiques.
    gabarit = a_remplacer.unique(subset=["EB_Flow", "EB_Product", "PEFA_Quadrant"], keep="first", maintain_order=True)
    avec_specifique = gabarit.join(
        specifiques.select(pl.col("flux_modele").alias("EB_Flow"), pl.col("produit_modele").alias("EB_Product"), "activite", "facteur"),
        on=["EB_Flow", "EB_Product"],
    )
    sans_specifique = gabarit.join(
        specifiques.select(pl.col("flux_modele").alias("EB_Flow"), pl.col("produit_modele").alias("EB_Product")).unique(),
        on=["EB_Flow", "EB_Product"], how="anti",
    ).join(generales.select(pl.col("flux_modele").alias("EB_Flow"), "activite", "facteur"), on="EB_Flow")
    remplacees = pl.concat([avec_specifique, sans_specifique]).with_columns(
        pl.col("activite").alias("PEFA_Target_Activity"), pl.col("facteur").alias("Allocation Factor")
    ).select(defaut.columns)
    conservees = defaut.filter(~pl.col("EB_Flow").is_in(flux_couverts.implode()))
    return pl.concat([conservees, remplacees])


ANNEES = sorted(cles["annee"].unique().to_list())
tunisie = pl.concat(
    [
        matrice_tunisienne(defaut, cles.filter(pl.col("annee") == a).drop("annee", "methode")).with_columns(
            annee=pl.lit(a, pl.Int16)
        )
        for a in ANNEES
    ]
)
tunisie.filter(pl.col("annee") == 2022).group_by("annee").len()

Each covered flow and product must keep factors that add up to 1 in the Tunisian matrix, for each quadrant and each target product.

couverts = tunisie.filter(pl.col("EB_Flow").is_in(correspondance["flux_modele"].unique().implode()))
sommes = couverts.group_by("annee", "EB_Flow", "EB_Product", "PEFA_Target_Product", "PEFA_Quadrant").agg(
    pl.col("Allocation Factor").sum()
)
assert (sommes["Allocation Factor"] - 1).abs().max() < 1e-9
print(f"{sommes.height} combinaisons contrôlées, facteurs entre {sommes['Allocation Factor'].min():.6f} et {sommes['Allocation Factor'].max():.6f}")

title: Concordance matrix and bridging items
text:
4 Differences from the default matrix
The following table compares, for each flow present in the Tunisian balance, the activity of the default matrix and the Tunisian activity, mapped back to its section. Rows marked oui (yes) in the column section_modifiee change the result of the tool, even at section level. The others only add industry detail.

flux_tunisiens = modele.select("flux_modele", "produit_modele").unique()
defaut_tunisien = defaut.join(flux_tunisiens, left_on=["EB_Flow", "EB_Product"], right_on=["flux_modele", "produit_modele"])
par_defaut_produit = defaut_tunisien.group_by("EB_Flow", "EB_Product").agg(
    pl.col("PEFA_Target_Activity").unique().sort().str.join(", ").alias("defaut_produit")
)
# Pour la correspondance générale d'un flux, les produits qui ont une correspondance propre sont exclus.
propres = correspondance.filter(pl.col("produit_modele").is_not_null()).select(
    pl.col("flux_modele").alias("EB_Flow"), pl.col("produit_modele").alias("EB_Product")
)
par_defaut = defaut_tunisien.join(propres, on=["EB_Flow", "EB_Product"], how="anti").group_by("EB_Flow").agg(
    pl.col("PEFA_Target_Activity").unique().sort().str.join(", ").alias("defaut_flux")
)
sections = dict(zip(activites["code"], activites["section_fmi"]))
tunisiennes = (
    correspondance.with_columns(section=pl.col("activite").replace_strict(sections))
    .group_by("flux_modele", "produit_modele", "justification", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(
        pl.col("activite").str.join(", ").alias("tunisie"),
        pl.col("section").unique().sort().str.join(", ").alias("sections_tunisie"),
    )
)
differences = (
    tunisiennes.join(par_defaut, left_on="flux_modele", right_on="EB_Flow", how="left")
    .join(par_defaut_produit, left_on=["flux_modele", "produit_modele"], right_on=["EB_Flow", "EB_Product"], how="left")
    .with_columns(defaut=pl.coalesce("defaut_produit", "defaut_flux"))
    .with_columns(
        section_modifiee=pl.when(pl.col("defaut") == pl.col("sections_tunisie")).then(pl.lit("non")).otherwise(pl.lit("oui"))
    )
    .select("flux_modele", "produit_modele", "defaut", "sections_tunisie", "section_modifiee", "tunisie", "justification")
)
differences.filter(pl.col("section_modifiee") == "oui")

For production and losses, the default matrix assigns each product to an activity, and the comparison is made product by product. The full table is saved with the matrix.






NoteOpen question



The choices that depart from the tool sections are to be validated with INS and ONEM. Electricity autoproducers and recovered heat are classified in the chemical industry. Solar heat is produced by households. Charcoal kilns belong to forestry. Non-energy uses are assigned to construction. Road transport and services are allocated by keys.

title: Concordance matrix and bridging items
text:
5 Bridging items

5.1 International bunkers
The ONEM balance gives international bunkers by product. The greenhouse gas inventory also gives bunker fuel, in TJ, in the memo items of category 1.D. For aviation bunkers, the two sources agree within 1% every year. Marine bunkers, which are much smaller, differ more in some years. The balance remains the source for PEFA, and the difference is to be examined with ANME for the emissions accounts.

crt = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/crt.parquet")
soutes_crt = (
    crt.filter(pl.col("crt").str.starts_with("1.D.1"), pl.col("parametre") == "activity", pl.col("unite") == "TJ")
    .with_columns(flux_modele=pl.when(pl.col("crt") == "1.D.1.a").then(pl.lit("International aviation bunkers")).otherwise(pl.lit("International marine bunkers")))
    .group_by("annee", "flux_modele").agg(pl.col("valeur").sum().alias("crt_tj"))
)
soutes_bilan = (
    modele.filter(pl.col("flux_modele").str.starts_with("International"))
    .group_by("annee", "flux_modele").agg((-pl.col("tj").sum()).alias("bilan_tj"))
)
soutes = (
    soutes_bilan.join(soutes_crt, on=["annee", "flux_modele"], how="full", coalesce=True)
    .with_columns(ecart_pct=((pl.col("bilan_tj") / pl.col("crt_tj") - 1) * 100).round(2))
    .sort("flux_modele", "annee")
)
assert soutes.filter(pl.col("flux_modele") == "International aviation bunkers")["ecart_pct"].abs().max() < 1
soutes.with_columns(pl.col("bilan_tj", "crt_tj").round(0))

The tool assigns bunkers to resident carriers in the transport industry. This assumption is kept for lack of information. Part of the bunkers is bought in Tunisia by non-resident carriers, which count as exports in the accounts.


5.2 Residence adjustments
The accounts follow the residence principle of the national accounts. Fuel bought abroad by resident units is added to imports and to their uses. Fuel bought in Tunisia by non-residents is added to exports. The tool receives these quantities in the Bridging_Items sheet, by PEFA product. No Tunisian source provides them for now; the range stays empty, as in the workbook supplied with the tool.

ponts = plages["EB_Bridging_Items"]
valeurs = [x for ligne in ponts[1:] for x in ligne[2:12] if isinstance(x, float) and x != 0]
assert not valeurs, "Des éléments de passage sont renseignés : les traiter dans la couche explicite"
print(f"Feuille Bridging_Items : {len(ponts) - 1} lignes, aucune quantité renseignée")







NoteOpen question



What data can INS or ONEM provide on fuel bought abroad by resident carriers and on fuel bought in Tunisia by non-residents? The OECD data on air and maritime transport, included in the I2A tool, cover Tunisia and could serve as a first estimate.

differences.write_parquet("data/intermediaires/concordance_differences.parquet", compression="zstd")
print(f"{SORTIE} : {tunisie.height} lignes pour {len(ANNEES)} années")

title: Checks, indicators and export of the PEFA
text:
1 Purpose
This page checks the PEFA computed on the previous page, compares them with the SUT for plausibility, computes energy intensities by industry and exports everything to an Excel workbook in French, English and Arabic.

from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import xlsxwriter

CODES = {"code": pl.String, "activite": pl.String}
KTEP_EN_TJ = 41.868
PRODUITS = Path("data/produits")
NOM = "comptes_pefa"

pefa = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/pefa.parquet")
modele = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/bilan_modele_fmi.parquet")
tre = pl.read_parquet("data/intermediaires/tre.parquet")
activites = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/activites.csv", schema_overrides=CODES)
lignes = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/pefa_lignes.csv")
libelles = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/libelles.csv")
ANNEES = sorted(pefa["annee"].unique().to_list())

# Codes d'activité de l'outil et codes du site
PSEUDO = ["RDM", "ACC", "ENV", "ECART"]
CODE_SITE = dict(activites.filter(pl.col("code").is_in(PSEUDO)).select("section_fmi", "code").iter_rows())
pefa = pefa.with_columns(pl.col("activite").replace(CODE_SITE))
CODE_SITE

title: Checks, indicators and export of the PEFA
text:
2 Balance of supply and use
In a PEFA table, each category of flows is balanced. The natural inputs supplied by the environment equal those used by industries, and the residuals generated equal the residuals absorbed by the environment or accumulated. For energy products, supply equals use apart from the rounding of the balance.

par_categorie = (
    pefa.group_by("annee", "niveau1")
    .agg(
        pl.col("tj").filter(pl.col("quadrant") == "Supply").sum().alias("ressources_tj"),
        pl.col("tj").filter(pl.col("quadrant") == "Use").sum().alias("emplois_tj"),
    )
    .with_columns(ecart_ktep=((pl.col("ressources_tj") - pl.col("emplois_tj")) / KTEP_EN_TJ).round(2))
)
par_categorie.pivot("niveau1", index="annee", values="ecart_ktep").sort("annee")


residus = par_categorie.filter(pl.col("niveau1") != "Energy products:")
assert residus["ecart_ktep"].abs().max() < 1e-6, "Ressources naturelles ou résidus déséquilibrés"

For energy products, the check is done product by product. The tool records all non-energy uses on a single row, whatever the product. In Tunisia, these uses concern only petroleum products, as the balance confirms. This row is therefore attached to oil for the check.

non_energetique = modele.filter(pl.col("flux_modele").str.starts_with("Non-energy use"))
petroliers = pl.read_csv("data/nomenclatures/bilan_produits.csv").filter(pl.col("parent") == "PP")["code"]
assert non_energetique["code_produit"].is_in(petroliers.implode()).all()

produits_energie = (
    pefa.filter(pl.col("niveau1") == "Energy products:")
    .with_columns(
        produit=pl.when(pl.col("produit") == "End-use of energy products for non-energy purposes").then(pl.lit("Oil")).otherwise("produit")
    )
    .group_by("annee", "produit")
    .agg(
        pl.col("tj").filter(pl.col("quadrant") == "Supply").sum().alias("ressources_tj"),
        pl.col("tj").filter(pl.col("quadrant") == "Use").sum().alias("emplois_tj"),
    )
    .with_columns(ecart_ktep=((pl.col("ressources_tj") - pl.col("emplois_tj")) / KTEP_EN_TJ).round(2))
)
assert produits_energie["ecart_ktep"].abs().max() <= 5, "Écart supérieur à l'arrondi du bilan"
produits_energie.pivot("produit", index="annee", values="ecart_ktep").sort("annee")

The remaining differences come from the rounding to the ktoe of the published cells of the balance, already noted on page 10. Oil groups ten balance products, whose rounding adds up; the tolerance is therefore 5 ktoe.

title: Checks, indicators and export of the PEFA
text:
3 Plausibility against the SUT
An industry that uses energy must buy, in the SUT, crude oil and natural gas (product 06), refined petroleum products (19) or electricity and gas (35). The SUT are in value, so the comparison looks at sign and order of magnitude. The ratio between the two gives an average implicit price, in dinars per gigajoule, which should stay within a reasonable range across industries.

ANNEE = ANNEES[-1]
SUT = set(activites.filter(~pl.col("code").is_in(PSEUDO + ["MEN"]))["code"])

energie_finale = (
    pefa.filter(
        pl.col("quadrant") == "Use",
        pl.col("niveau1") == "Energy products:",
        pl.col("niveau2") == "End-use of energy products by SIEC class:",
        pl.col("activite").is_in(list(SUT | {"MEN"})),
    )
    .group_by("annee", "activite")
    .agg(pl.col("tj").sum().alias("energie_tj"))
)
achats = (
    tre.filter(pl.col("bloc") == "emplois", pl.col("ligne").is_in(["06", "19", "35"]), ~pl.col("agregat"), pl.col("annee").is_in(ANNEES))
    .with_columns(activite=pl.when(pl.col("colonne") == "P3_MEN").then(pl.lit("MEN")).otherwise(pl.col("colonne")))
    .filter(pl.col("activite").is_in(list(SUT | {"MEN"})))
    .group_by("annee", "activite")
    .agg(pl.col("valeur").sum().alias("achats_mdt"))
)
vraisemblance = (
    energie_finale.join(achats, on=["annee", "activite"], how="full", coalesce=True)
    .with_columns(pl.col("energie_tj", "achats_mdt").fill_null(0))
    .with_columns(prix_tnd_gj=(pl.col("achats_mdt") * 1e6 / (pl.col("energie_tj") * 1e3)).round(1))
    .join(activites.select(pl.col("code").alias("activite"), "fr"), on="activite")
)
vraisemblance.filter(pl.col("annee") == ANNEE).sort("energie_tj", descending=True).with_columns(
    pl.col("energie_tj", "achats_mdt").round(0)
)

Refining (19) and electricity (35) have a high implicit price, because their purchases of energy products are mostly transformation inputs, which are excluded here from end use. Industries that consume energy without buying any in the SUT, or the reverse, need to be examined; the following table lists them.

vraisemblance.filter(
    ((pl.col("energie_tj") > 0) & (pl.col("achats_mdt") <= 0)) | ((pl.col("energie_tj") <= 0) & (pl.col("achats_mdt") > 0))
).select("annee", "activite", "fr", "energie_tj", "achats_mdt").sort("activite", "annee")







NoteOpen question



Very high or very low implicit prices point to an allocation that needs review. Service industries receive the services energy according to their purchases of electricity and gas; their implicit price mostly reflects this key. Industries that buy petroleum products without receiving energy from the balance (for example for their vehicles) depend on the road transport key. These points are to be discussed with INS during the mission.

title: Checks, indicators and export of the PEFA
text:
4 Energy intensities
The energy intensity of an industry relates its energy end use (excluding transformation inputs) to its output or value added, in terajoules per million current dinars. These indicators follow the SUT at current prices, so their changes combine volumes and prices.

comptes_production = (
    tre.filter(pl.col("bloc") == "valeur_ajoutee", pl.col("ligne").is_in(["P1", "B1G"]))
    .pivot("ligne", index=["annee", "colonne"], values="valeur")
    .rename({"colonne": "activite", "P1": "production_mdt", "B1G": "valeur_ajoutee_mdt"})
)
indicateurs = (
    energie_finale.filter(pl.col("activite") != "MEN")
    .join(comptes_production, on=["annee", "activite"], how="left")
    .with_columns(
        intensite_production=pl.col("energie_tj") / pl.col("production_mdt"),
        intensite_va=pl.col("energie_tj") / pl.col("valeur_ajoutee_mdt"),
    )
    .rename({"energie_tj": "energie_finale_tj"})
    .sort("annee", "activite")
)
(
    indicateurs.filter(pl.col("annee") == ANNEE)
    .join(activites.select(pl.col("code").alias("activite"), "fr"), on="activite")
    .select("activite", "fr", pl.col("energie_finale_tj").round(0), pl.col("intensite_va").round(2))
    .sort("intensite_va", descending=True)
)

title: Checks, indicators and export of the PEFA
text:
5 Export
The workbook contains a notes sheet, the long table for all years, one supply sheet and one use sheet per year, and the indicators. Row labels come from data/nomenclatures/pefa_lignes.csv, activity labels from data/nomenclatures/activites.csv, and headers from data/nomenclatures/libelles.csv. The Arabic sheets run from right to left.

ORDRE_ACTIVITES = activites["code"].to_list()
ORDRE_LIGNES = {(t, c): o for t, c, o in lignes.select("type", "cle", "ordre").iter_rows()}


def traduire(langue: str) -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:
    t = dict(zip(libelles["cle"], libelles[langue]))
    l = dict(zip(lignes["cle"], lignes[langue]))
    a = dict(zip(activites["code"], activites[langue]))
    return t, l, a


def matrice(annee: int, quadrant: str, langue: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Tableau des ressources ou des emplois d'une année : produits en lignes, activités en colonnes."""
    t, l, a = traduire(langue)
    donnees = pefa.filter(pl.col("annee") == annee, pl.col("quadrant") == quadrant)
    presentes = [c for c in ORDRE_ACTIVITES if c in set(donnees["activite"])]
    tableau = (
        donnees.with_columns(
            o1=pl.col("niveau1").replace_strict({c: o for (ty, c), o in ORDRE_LIGNES.items() if ty == "niveau1"}),
            o2=pl.col("niveau2").replace_strict({c: o for (ty, c), o in ORDRE_LIGNES.items() if ty == "niveau2"}, default=0),
            o3=pl.col("produit").replace_strict({c: o for (ty, c), o in ORDRE_LIGNES.items() if ty == "produit"}),
        )
        .pivot("activite", index=["o1", "o2", "o3", "niveau1", "niveau2", "produit"], values="tj", aggregate_function="sum")
        .sort("o1", "o2", "o3")
    )
    tableau = tableau.with_columns(pl.col(presentes).fill_null(0)).with_columns(
        pl.sum_horizontal(presentes).alias("total")
    )
    return tableau.select(
        pl.col("niveau1").replace_strict(l).alias(t["niveau1"]),
        pl.col("niveau2").replace_strict(l, default=None).alias(t["niveau2"]),
        pl.col("produit").replace_strict(l).alias(t["produit"]),
        *[pl.col(c).alias(f"{c} {a[c]}") for c in presentes],
        pl.col("total").alias(t["total"]),
    )


def donnees_longues(langue: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    t, l, a = traduire(langue)
    return pefa.select(
        pl.col("annee").alias(t["annee"]),
        pl.col("quadrant").replace_strict({"Supply": t["Supply"], "Use": t["Use"]}).alias(t["quadrant"]),
        pl.col("niveau1").replace_strict(l).alias(t["niveau1"]),
        pl.col("niveau2").replace_strict(l, default=None).alias(t["niveau2"]),
        pl.col("produit").replace_strict(l).alias(t["produit"]),
        pl.col("activite").alias(t["code_activite"]),
        pl.col("activite").replace_strict(a).alias(t["activite"]),
        pl.col("tj").alias(t["tj"]),
    )


def indicateurs_traduits(langue: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    t, l, a = traduire(langue)
    return indicateurs.select(
        pl.col("annee").alias(t["annee"]),
        pl.col("activite").alias(t["code_activite"]),
        pl.col("activite").replace_strict(a).alias(t["activite"]),
        *[pl.col(c).alias(t[c]) for c in ["energie_finale_tj", "production_mdt", "valeur_ajoutee_mdt", "intensite_production", "intensite_va"]],
    )


def exporter(langue: str) -> Path:
    t, _, _ = traduire(langue)
    dossier = PRODUITS / langue
    dossier.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    chemin = dossier / f"{NOM}.xlsx"
    with xlsxwriter.Workbook(chemin) as classeur:
        notes = classeur.add_worksheet(t["feuille_notes"])
        for i, cle in enumerate(["titre_pefa", "unite_tj", "note_source", "note_methode", "note_provisoire", "note_site"]):
            notes.write(i, 0, t[cle])
        feuilles = [(t["feuille_donnees"], donnees_longues(langue), 1)]
        for annee in ANNEES:
            feuilles.append((f"{t['feuille_ressources']} {annee}", matrice(annee, "Supply", langue), 1))
            feuilles.append((f"{t['feuille_emplois']} {annee}", matrice(annee, "Use", langue), 1))
        feuilles.append((t["feuille_indicateurs"], indicateurs_traduits(langue), 3))
        for nom, tableau, decimales in feuilles:
            tableau.write_excel(workbook=classeur, worksheet=nom, autofit=True, float_precision=decimales)
        if langue == "ar":
            for feuille in classeur.worksheets():
                feuille.right_to_left()
    return chemin


for langue in ["fr", "en", "ar"]:
    print(exporter(langue))
